title: Modular Exponentiation
prompt:
Compute the modular power:

    7^128 mod 13

Reduce to its least non-negative residue. (Hint: Fermat's little theorem says 7^12 ≡ 1 (mod 13), so reduce the exponent mod 12 first.)
hint: enter a single whole number in the range 0 .. 12
recap:
Modular exponentiation a^b mod m uses square-and-multiply in O(log b) steps, never forming a^b. Fermat's little theorem helps for prime m with gcd(a, m) = 1: a^(m-1) ≡ 1, so reduce the exponent mod (m − 1).

Example — 7^128 mod 13: 128 ≡ 8 (mod 12), so it is 7^8; squaring, 7²≡10, 7⁴≡9, 7⁸≡81≡3 (mod 13).

Reference: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms, §31.6.
